# Audit runner leaves items at open/plan_complete after a failing/aborted audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update)

## Problem statement

During an audit, `audit_runner.py` transitions the target item out of
`completed`/`in_review` (to `in-progress`/`in_review` or `open`/`plan_complete`)
and is supposed to **restore it to `completed`/`in_review`** on every exit path
(the abort path logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`).

Under concurrency this restore is **lost**: a `wl sync` running in another
session (or the audit runner's own sync) races the restore, and the item is
left stuck at `open`/`plan_complete` (status `open`, stage `plan_complete`,
`auditResult: null`). The item silently drops out of the release candidate set
(`stage: in_review`) and looks like brand-new, un-implemented work — a
**worklog data-integrity regression**, not a cosmetic glitch.

This is the same class as the known concurrent-`wl sync` lost-update race
(WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); the audit runner's own status restore is not
race-safe against it.

## Users

- **Release operators** running `/skill:ship release` — corrupted items silently
  drop out of the release candidate set, causing releases to omit valid items or
  include items that failed audit.
- **Agents** implementing work — an item left at `open`/`plan_complete` looks
  like un-implemented work and may be picked up for re-implementation.
- **Producer reviewers** — corrupted items appear in the wrong state in the
  worklog dashboard and reports.

## Observed (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising `/skill:ship release`)

A single release attempt corrupted **four** items, each left at
`open`/`plan_complete` although all four were `completed`/`in_review` before:

| Item | Corrupted by | Prior state (from worklog-data history) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RISE-0MVWWBT8Y009FMZ6` | release gate audit remediation (14:00) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3MXVU5009GMLR` | `--refresh-audits` (14:38) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:57) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:59) | `completed`/`in_review` |

All four were repaired by hand (`wl update <id> --status completed --stage
in_review`) after reconstructing the prior state from the `refs/worklog/...`
delta history. The corruption spans both the failing-verdict path (a
persisted "Ready to close: No" still left the item at `open`/`plan_complete`)
and the aborted path (the "restoring" message logged but the restore did not
persist).

## Root-cause hypotheses to confirm

- The restore is a plain `wl update` with no compare-and-swap / version guard,
  so a concurrent `wl sync` (pull→merge→push) overwrites it (last-writer-wins
  on a stale snapshot).
- A failing/aborted audit may not run the restore at all on some exit paths
  (the observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict
  suggests the restore is skipped when the verdict is not "Yes").

## Desired change

Make the audit runner's status restore **race-safe and unconditional**:

- Restore `completed`/`in_review` on **every** exit path — success, failing
  verdict, abort, exception, timeout — via `try/finally`.
- Use the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  and its claim/assignee handling so the restore participates in the same
  lost-update protection as other lifecycle exits.
- Guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (e.g. re-read after write,
  retry on mismatch — the same verification pattern the ship skill uses for
  close verification, SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- Never leave an item at `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed
  — a failing verdict is recorded while the item stays `completed`/`in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict demotes the item to `open`/`plan_complete` deliberately and verified (this is the audit-reject contract); an infra-fallback-tainted, aborted, timed-out or crashed audit never demotes.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path via `try/finally`, including exceptions raised after the `in_progress` claim.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` or `in_progress` as a side effect of any audit path, and an unverified restore is never reported as success.

## Impact

Auditing an `in_review` item can no longer silently revert it to un-implemented
work, so release candidate sets and worklog state stay correct under
concurrent agent sessions.

## Constraints

- The audit runner's core auditing semantics (what gets audited, how verdicts
  are calculated) must not change — only the status-restore path is affected.
- The fix must not introduce additional contention on the worklog database
  that would slow down normal audit throughput.
- The restore must use the same `--worklog-dir` resolution as the rest of the
  audit runner (cwd-independent).

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py` transitions the target item to `open`/`plan_complete` at the
start of an audit and has restore logic on the abort path, but:
- The restore is not wrapped in `try/finally` (missing on some exit paths).
- The restore is a plain `wl update` — no re-read/verify/retry against concurrent
  `wl sync` (the same pattern fixed in SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- The failing-verdict path may skip the restore entirely.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Audit runner core; status transition and restore logic live here.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared lifecycle helper with claim/assignee semantics.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Reference for the close-verification retry pattern (SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — Test directory for audit runner tests.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — The `wl sync` helper that the race originates from.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5** — Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success (lost-update close verification pattern).
- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — wl sync --if-idle reverts actively-worked items to open/intake_complete (lost-update race fix).
- **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** — Only mark as complete when fully complete (adjacent lifecycle-transition safety).
- **SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ** — Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote in_review children (completed) (adjacent audit-raced-lifecycle-transition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The restore logic exists on the abort path but is lost to race — not completely absent. Needs code verification.
- **Risk:** Adding a retry loop to the restore could introduce subtle timing issues if the retry window overlaps with other concurrent operations.
- **Risk:** The fix must not change audit timing behaviour — agents must not see longer audit durations.
- **Scope creep:** Fixing the general `wl sync` lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) is out of scope; this item only fixes the audit runner's restore path.


## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-13)

Planning decision: **plan required** (effort Small / risk Medium — above the
auto-skip threshold). Approval gate not requested (only *Extra Large* effort
**and** *High/Severe* risk triggers an approval pause).

### Code inspection results (closes the two open questions in this item)

1. **"Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?"**
   Partly — and the reported symptom is (mostly) a misdiagnosis. A genuine
   explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict **deliberately demotes** to
   `open`/`plan_complete` (the audit-reject workflow: `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`
   'no' branch; documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` → Status Lifecycle;
   pinned by `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
   `test_ready_no_sets_open_plan_complete` and `test_audit_runner_core.py`
   "A 'No' verdict still demotes to open/plan_complete"). An
   **infra-fallback-tainted** `No`, a timeout, a provider error, a parse
   failure or a crash takes the **restore** branch and must never demote.
   The observed `open`/`plan_complete` items all had `auditResult: null`,
   i.e. the run never persisted a verdict — consistent with an aborted run
   whose restore was lost, not with a demoting `No`.
2. **"Does `StatusLifecycle` provide verify-then-retry?"** No. The in-run
   lifecycle verification/retry (3 attempts, linear backoff) lives in
   `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK), *not* in
   `StatusLifecycle`. Three restore paths are weaker or unverified:
   - `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` — one write, one readback, no retry.
   - `_restore_work_item_status` (SIGTERM/SIGINT handler) — one write, **no
     readback**.
   - `check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` — the parent-side
     SIGKILL recovery that logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring ...`:
     a bare `wl update`, **no readback, no retry**, and the state file is
     deleted even when the restore did not persist (so a lost update is
     unrecoverable). This is the exact log line quoted in the problem
     statement. The same gap applies to every other state-file consumer.
   - `cmd_issue`'s `finally` is entered *after* the `in_progress` claim in
     `_phase_gate`, so an exception between the claim and the `try`
     (`audit_lease_begin`, `_open_checkpoint_store`) leaves the claim behind.
   - `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` demotes as a *persist-time side
     effect* (worklog `revertToPlanComplete`), before the terminal
     lifecycle corrects it — an unguarded window on restore-bound runs
     (same class as SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ, fixed there for children only).

### Plan decision D1 — AC1 wording reconciled (producer confirmation requested)

AC1 as originally written ("a failing verdict leaves the item at
`completed`/`in_review` — never `open`/`plan_complete`") **contradicts the
documented, tested audit-reject contract** described above; implementing it
literally would remove the mechanism that returns rejected work to the
actionable queue, invalidate 8+ existing tests, and change release-gate
semantics. Evidence (source code and tests override the worklog text)
supports narrowing AC1 to: *an explicit `No` demotes deliberately and
verified; nothing else may demote, ever*. This is recorded as producer
question Q3 in the Appendix and the item carries `needsProducerReview`, so
the producer can overrule before the policy child is implemented. If
overruled, only child F4 (policy) and AC1 change — the three mechanical
fixes stand unchanged.

### Features (vertical slices, test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Race-clobber restore regression tests | task | Deterministic clobber injection (tests first, red before the fix) |
| F2 | Verified-retry in-run lifecycle restore | task | Python runner: settle-verify-retry on every restore path + claim inside the guard |
| F3 | Verified-retry parent-side abort restore | task | `check-audit-gate.js` state-file restore: readback + one retry + retained state file |
| F4 | Verdict-demotion policy documented and pinned | docs | Document reconciled contract; pin explicit-`No` demotion vs never-demote paths |

Each child is a deliverable end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs where
applicable). No horizontal layer phases are needed at this size.

### Requirement to feature mapping

| Requirement (this item) | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| Desired change 1 - restore on every exit path (`try/finally`, exceptions) | F2 (in-run, claim inside the guard), F3 (parent-side abort) |
| Desired change 2 - use the shared `StatusLifecycle` claim/assignee handling | F2 (key file + assignee-release semantics; reuse the shared claim-release predicate) |
| Desired change 3 - guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (re-read/retry) | F1 (red test), F2, F3 |
| Desired change 4 - never leave an item `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed (reconciled by D1: only a genuine explicit `No` demotes) | F2, F4 |
| AC1 (reworded by D1) | F2 (non-demoting paths) + F4 (contract pinned; awaits Q3) |
| AC4 (regression test injecting a concurrent `wl sync`) | F1 |
| Constraints - semantics unchanged, no added contention, cwd-independent `--worklog-dir` | F2 (explicit ACs); F3 (state-file dirs unchanged) |

### Traceability

- Duplicate check performed (`wl search` "restore race lifecycle", `wl search`
  "audit restore lost update"): no full duplicate. Precedents:
  SA-0MRNKVPTA005FKBG (restore-pre-audit-state), SA-0MTRH8C5O005URGR (abort
  recovery state file), SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5 (close verification), and the
  partially overlapping open idea SA-0MVIO0WQW006Y1FS (audit slot + verdict
  lifecycle idempotence) — related, not duplicate.
- Children F2/F3 depend on F1 (tests first); F4 depends on F2 and F3 (it
  documents the behaviour those slices land).

## Appendix

- Q: "Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?" — A: OPEN QUESTION — code inspection needed. The observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict suggests it does not.
- Q: "Does StatusLifecycle provide a mechanism for verify-then-retry on status restoration?" — A: To be confirmed — StatusLifecycle has claim/assignee handling; verify-then-retry may need to be added or handled externally (as the ship skill does).
- Q (Q1): "Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?" -
  **Answer (code inspection, plan 2026-11-13):** a genuine explicit `No`
  demotes **by design** (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` 'no' branch, documented in
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and pinned by `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`);
  infra-fallback/timeout/abort runs take the restore branch. The corrupted
  items had `auditResult: null`, i.e. no verdict was persisted - an aborted run
  with a lost restore, not a demoting `No`. Evidence:
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`,
  `_compute_fallback_tainted`), `skill/audit/SKILL.md` section "Status
  Lifecycle", `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`.
- Q (Q2): "Does `StatusLifecycle` provide verify-then-retry on status
  restoration?" - **Answer (plan 2026-11-13):** No. Verify-then-retry lives in
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (3 attempts, linear backoff, WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK).
  `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (single write, single readback),
  `_restore_work_item_status` (signal handler: write only) and
  `check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` (bare `wl update`, no
  readback, state file deleted regardless) are unprotected - the last one emits
  the exact `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring ...` line from the problem
  statement.
- Q (Q3, OPEN QUESTION - producer): "AC1 as written says a failing verdict must
  leave the item at `completed`/`in_review`, but the audit-reject contract
  (documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and covered by existing tests) requires
  a genuine explicit `No` to demote to `open`/`plan_complete`. Which wins?" -
  **Plan recommendation:** keep the documented demotion for a genuine explicit
  `No` (verified), and make every other path non-demoting (plan decision D1,
  AC1 reworded accordingly). Directed to: producer, because overruling would
  change release-gate/reject semantics. Matters because AC1 and child F4
  (policy documentation) depend on it.

## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** – Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs (completed)
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** – ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (pyproject.toml version source) (completed)

# Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** (residual post-fix slot-wait re-measurement follow-up).

## Problem statement

The `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` harness's genuine-run filter admits tool results from non-bash tools (e.g. `read`) when their text contains structural markers, so fixture text echoed by a file read is parsed as genuine slot-wait measurements — producing a spurious 999.0 s sample that fails the `no_run_over_120s` threshold.

## Target outcome

Fix the `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` false positive so that reading a fixture/source file can never be counted as a genuine test-slot run, restoring a trustworthy `no_run_over_120s` verdict.

## Users

- **Producer / agent operators** running the slot-wait re-measurement harness to verify the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix removed test-slot starvation. A false-positive breach invalidates their verdict and blocks RCA closure.
- Example user story: *As a producer closing the slot-starvation RCA (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV), I need the harness verdict to reflect only real runs, so that a `fail` genuinely means users are still waiting > 120 s for a slot.*

## Existing state (evidence, 2026-11-10)

Running `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window reports a spurious **999.0 s** `dev_push_gate` sample. It is an artefact, not a run:

- An agent `read` `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (session record `2026-11-10T15:23:02.987Z`).
- That file contains the fixture text `"slot_wait_seconds": 999.0` plus a `run_tests: gate-subject` marker.
- The harness's genuine-run filter trusts a tool result whose text carries a structural marker when no bash command is resolvable. A `read` tool result has no bash command, so the fixture text is parsed as **four fake gate samples** (122.687, 9.0, 1.25, 999.0).
- Effect: `dev_push_gate` inflates from 5 calls / max 0.002 s to 9 calls / max 999.0 s, and `no_run_over_120s` fails on a non-existent run.

Reproduction (confirmed): `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import measure_slot_wait as m; print(m.parse_block(open('tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py').read())['gate'])"` — prints the four injected samples.

Root cause: `measure()` pairs each `toolResult` with its assistant `toolCall` command via `_commands_by_tool_call`, which maps **only `bash` tool calls**. A `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep` result therefore resolves to `command=None` and falls through to the `_has_structural_marker` fallback intended for genuine bash runs whose call record is missing (forked/compacted logs).

## Desired change

Distinguish "no command resolvable because the log is incomplete" from "no command because the result came from a non-bash tool". The `toolResult` message itself carries `toolName`; only `bash` results (or a result with no tool name) may use the structural-marker fallback. A result whose `toolName` is a non-bash tool is never a measurement, regardless of its text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `read` (or any non-bash tool) result that merely echoes fixture text is never counted as a genuine run sample.
2. A regression test proves reading `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (and a generic fixture file) injects zero samples.
3. The genuine-run filter still accepts real run sources (`run_tests.py`, `implement.py`, `git push`, `wait_for_job.py`) and genuine structural-marker results with no resolvable command.
4. `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window no longer reports the 999.0 s sample.
5. Testing/validation criterion: the regression test fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The slot-wait re-measurement harness stops reporting phantom breaches, so the parent RCA's threshold verdict is trustworthy.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement tooling; never synthesise load.
- No change to the lane ceilings or threshold values.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — genuine-run filter in `measure()`; also the module docstring's "Attribution — genuine run filter" section.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — regression test for the fixture-echo false positive.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — "Genuine-run filter" paragraph (needs the bash-only rule stated).

## Related work

- `SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU` — the follow-up item whose re-measurement surfaced this artefact.
- `SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K` — the harness's originating item.
- `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` — parent; its AC3 threshold check is the consumer of this verdict.
- `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI` — ruff ISC004 flagging `measure_slot_wait.py`; same file, unrelated lint false-positive, do not conflate with this fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix must not tighten acceptance for valid cases — genuine structural-marker results from bash runs with missing call records must still pass.
- **Confirmed assumption**: `toolResult` messages carry a `toolName` field set to `"bash"` on genuine bash tool results. Verified across a ~3,000-result sample of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: `bash` 2346, `read` 394, `edit` 251, `write` 56, `grep` 17, `skill_path` 1 — every genuine run source is `bash`, so a `toolName != "bash"` guard is safe.
- **Assumption**: no non-bash tool legitimately carries slot-wait data in its result text.
- **Scope-creep risk**: do not extend the fix to other measurement harnesses (`measure_audit_performance.py`) unless they exhibit the same pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the work item description provides sufficient evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria to proceed. Verified independently: (a) the reproduction prints the four injected gate samples; (b) `toolName` is present and `bash`-only for genuine runs across the session corpus; (c) the "Genuine-run filter" docs paragraph is the only prose describing the fallback.

# Replace bare `except`-`pass` with exception logging in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` contains a `try`-`except` block in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` that catches all exceptions from `git for-each-ref` and silently passes. This hides diagnostic information about why feature branch resolution failed, making it harder to debug merge-gate issues in production.

## Users

- **Agent auditors**: When the merge gate fails to resolve feature branches, the silent pass means the failure reason is lost — the audit proceeds but with silently missing evidence.
- **Maintainers debugging audit failures**: Without exception details, diagnosing why a specific work item's branch refs could not be resolved requires reproducing the exact failure conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The bare `except Exception: pass` in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` (feature-branch resolution section, ~line 11799) is replaced with a `print` to `sys.stderr` that reports the issue ID and exception details, while retaining fail-open semantics.
2. The `noqa: S110` directive is removed (the bare pass no longer exists).
3. The `noqa: BLE001` directive is retained (the exception is still swallowed to stay fail-open).
4. The change is a single-function edit (replacing `pass` with a `print` call and binding the exception via `as exc`).
5. No functional behaviour change — the merge gate still fails open when ref resolution fails.

## Impact

Audit agents can now see *why* feature-branch resolution failed, improving debuggability of merge-gate evidence gaps.

## Constraints

- Must use the same `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` pattern already established in this file.
- Must not change any return values, function signature, or upstream callers.
- Must not introduce any new dependencies or imports.

## Existing state

```python
except Exception:  # noqa: S110, BLE001 -- best-effort; never fail the gate on ref resolution
    pass
```

The surrounding function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` resolves feature branches and commit SHAs for merge-gate verification. It is called by the merge-gate verification code which already prints success/failure diagnostics to stderr.

## Desired change

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- best-effort; never fail the gate on ref resolution
    print(
        f"Merge gate: ref resolution for {issue_id} failed — "
        f"git for-each-ref error: {exc}",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
```

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Single exception handler edit in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`

## Related work

- Multiple similar S110 items completed in `audit_runner.py` (SA-0MS3ATEOP005DRAD line 1039, SA-0MS3ATFSJ007GHRB line 1678, SA-0MS3ATGCE002WE91 line 1805).
- The same S110 pattern appears elsewhere in the codebase addressed in separate items.

## Appendix

- Q: What logging pattern to use? — Answer: `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` consistent with existing merge-gate output at line ~12553. Source: codebase scan of audit_runner.py stderr patterns.

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Problem statement

A contended host aborts a green unit stage with exit 124 and a diagnostic that (a) describes only
the browser failure mode and (b) prints the **elapsed** time in the sentence that reads as the
**bound**, so an operator cannot tell contention from a genuine hang without opening the cache
entry and re-deriving the numbers by hand.

## Users

- **Release producer** (primary): "When a release aborts in the unit stage I want the log to tell
  me the host was at load 38 on 16 cores and the stage ran 312 s against a 300 s bound, so I retry
  instead of bisecting a green suite."
- **Release producer on an idle host**: "When the unit stage aborts at load 0.4 against a 300 s
  bound, I want the diagnostic to point at a synchronous loop in test/engine code, not at
  `requestAnimationFrame`."
- **CI operator on a small host**: "I want the bound to stay an explicit, overridable number so a
  4-core runner is not handed a bound calibrated for a 16-core workstation."

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Existing state (verified in this intake pass, 2026-11-14)

All line numbers verified against the TCE checkout at `main` @ `70b4981f`.

- **The diagnostic takes only the elapsed time.** `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` at
  `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221` builds the line
  `[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within ${elapsedSecs}s` — the bound (`timeoutMs`) is
  never passed in, so the printed number is elapsed wall time wearing the bound's clothes. This is
  the conflation the ACs call out.
- **Two of three hang messages have the defect.** `listHangMessage` (line 237, pre-flight
  `vitest list`) is the same shape; its bound is the constant `LIST_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`
  (line 217). The third message, the coverage-preflight fallback at line 492, already prints the
  *bound* (`Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)`) — so the codebase is inconsistent rather than uniformly
  wrong, and the fix should unify all three on one shape.
- **Both inputs are already in scope at the call sites.** `runVitestProcess` owns `opts.timeoutMs`
  (the timer at line 1173) and returns `elapsedSecs` (line 1184); the two abort paths
  (`runVitestAsync` line 1214, `runVitestListAsync` line 1246) therefore have bound *and* elapsed
  in hand — the work is threading them into the message plus adding stage and load.
- **Stage is implicit, not first-class.** Nothing in the runner models a stage: `--project unit`
  and `--project browser` are forwarded argv from `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` and `:96`. A stage
  value must either be threaded from the caller or derived from the forwarded args, and it must
  cover the pre-flight `vitest list` too (which forwards the same args).
- **The header comment is already stale.** `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:59` says "5 min for unit
  (nominal <2 min)"; the measured worst green unit stage is 217 s — 72 % of the 300 s bound, not
  "<2 min". The rationale cannot be corrected without the measured baseline being recorded beside
  it, which is why the documentation AC is in scope rather than cosmetic.
- **The outer budget has *zero* slack today, not 4–7 min.** `.pi/test-config.json` sets
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, applied by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:4551`
  (`args.timeout or suite_timeout_per_command(...) or 600`) to the **single** `npm --silent test`
  command that runs the whole of `run-ci-tests.sh`. Today's stage bounds already sum to
  **300 + 1200 = 1500 s — exactly the outer bound** — and that sum excludes the terminology guard,
  the browser-env pre-check, both `vitest list` pre-flights, the shell orchestration, and the
  (unbounded) Tutorial E2E stage. The 4–7 min of headroom in the original AC is measured against
  the *nominal 18–21 min runtime*, not against the sum of bounds, so it does not cover a raise.
  Any raised or scaled unit bound therefore **must** raise `timeoutPerCommand` in the same change
  (e.g. a 600 s floor ⇒ 1800 s of stage bounds ⇒ outer ≈ 2100–2400 s).
- **An over-budget command is reported separately from a hang.** `run_tests.py` emits the
  `suite_timeout` notice (`NOTICE_SUITE_TIMEOUT`, lines 240 / 3247) — the outer and inner bounds
  must not become confusable in the abort log.
- **The test seam pattern already exists.** `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (1353
  lines) injects runners, `binPath` and `killGraceMs`; `runVitestProcess` takes an injectable
  `opts` bag. The load average and core count should follow that same injection style.

## Desired change

1. One shared hang-diagnostic builder that always prints **stage, configured bound, elapsed wall
   time, the delta over the bound, host load average at abort and core count** — used by the run
   abort, the pre-flight `vitest list` abort and the coverage-preflight fallback.
2. Stage-appropriate guidance: the `requestAnimationFrame` / undestroyed `Phaser.Game` /
   "run one file under `--project browser`" paragraph is browser-only; a unit-stage abort instead
   points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code. The pre-flight gets the abbreviated form.
3. A unit-stage bound derived as **hybrid**: a raised static floor (justified against the measured
   baseline) plus load-aware scaling from the sampled 1-min load average relative to core count,
   clamped to a finite ceiling, still overridable with `--timeout-ms`.
4. A corrected outer budget (`.pi/test-config.json`) and a corrected rationale in the
   `run-ci-tests.sh` header and the TCE hang-timeout docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` /
  `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time,
  the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention
  is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry. All three hang messages
  (run abort, pre-flight `vitest list` abort, coverage-preflight fallback) share one builder, so the
  current elapsed-as-bound wording at `hangTimeoutMessage`/`listHangMessage` is gone and bound,
  elapsed, stage and load are rendered identically everywhere.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound) **plus load-aware scaling** of the bound from the
  sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**; the bound
  remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`), and `--timeout-ms` still wins over the computed
  bound.
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout — today the bounds already sum to exactly
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` (300 + 1200) with zero slack, so raising or scaling an inner bound
  either adjusts `.pi/test-config.json` in the same change or documents, with the arithmetic, why
  it still fits.
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline (88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149,
  206, 217 s) are recorded in the `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` and `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  header comments — replacing the falsified "5 min for unit (nominal <2 min)" — and in the TCE
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
- The release gate documents the behaviour on this repo's side: `docs/dev/release-tests.md` gains a
  short "hang abort vs host contention" note stating that a stall is reported as exit 124 with the
  stage/bound/elapsed/load diagnostic, and that a contended-host abort is never auto-retried and
  must be re-run once the host is quiet.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; the
  computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average and core count are injected through a
  test seam and are never read from the real host; cases cover an idle host (floor applies), a
  loaded host (scaling applies), and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus a browser-stage message
  containing no unit-stage guidance and vice versa.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor. `os.loadavg()` is meaningless on Windows — the runner must degrade to the static floor
  there rather than compute a bogus scale.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average or core count in a test; sample it
  behind an injectable seam (the `runVitestProcess` `opts` bag / injected-runner pattern already in
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`).
- **Log noise budget.** The per-attempt `[vitest-runner] ... attempts=N status=S outcome=...` line
  is parsed by release-gate tooling and by `run_tests.py`'s notice classification — the new
  diagnostic enriches the `[hang-timeout]` block and must not break the `[vitest-runner]` line's
  shape.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption.** Load average at abort is sampled *after* the kill, from the parent runner
  process; it is an indicator of contention during the run, not a measurement integrated over it.
  If a more faithful signal (per-attempt max load) turns out cheap to capture, that is an
  implementation choice for the plan, not a new AC.

## Key Files (predicted)

- **Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here)**
  - `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — `hangTimeoutMessage` (line 221) / `listHangMessage`
    (line 237) / the fallback at line 492 unified into one stage-aware builder; load-average +
    core-count sampling seam; hybrid bound derivation (floor + load scale + ceiling) around
    `DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (line 188) and `parseRunnerArgs`' `--timeout-ms` (line 322).
  - `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — unit stage `--timeout-ms` (line 92) raised to the new floor;
    header rationale (line ~51–59) corrected against the measured baseline.
  - `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — diagnostic-content assertions and
    floor/scaling/ceiling cases with an injected load average and core count.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
  - `.pi/test-config.json` — `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` adjusted in the same change as any raised
    unit bound (see the outer-budget AC).
- **This repo (framework)**
  - `docs/dev/release-tests.md` — new "hang abort vs host contention" note (66-line file;
    "How the merge is gated on success" / "Re-running after a fix" are the natural anchors).
  - `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — gate log surface / comments (~line 340–356)
    if the abort is to be surfaced distinctly from a red suite.
  - `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `timeoutPerCommand` handling (line 1488/4551) and the
    `suite_timeout` notice (line 240/3247); read-only unless the outer/inner distinction needs to
    appear in its output.

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.

- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this

- Sibling item: **SA-0MWEURY420040OMD** (this repo, `intake_complete`) — the green-cache-entry

- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** (this repo, completed) — browser-suite contention: two concurrent full

- **Q1 (bound strategy: A static raise / B load-aware only / C hybrid) — ANSWERED: C (hybrid).**

- **Re-intake verification (2026-11-14, Map, SA-0MWEURUYL004I470) — no new questions asked.** The
  brief was re-verified against the trees rather than re-interviewed; every claim above now carries
  a file:line anchor. Findings that changed the brief: (a) the diagnostic's defect is exactly
  `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs)` printing elapsed time as the bound (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221`);
  (b) a third hang message at line 492 already prints the bound, so the fix unifies rather than

  Issue type (`feature`) and priority (`high`) re-confirmed; no operator input required.
## Plan (2026-11-14, Map — `/skill:plan`)

**Effort:** Medium (PERT expected 48.7 h, recommended 70.7 h) · **Risk:** Medium (score 11/25,

### Design decisions the plan owns

- **D1 — Implementation stays in place in TCE.** The bounded runner remains
  `Tableau-Card-Engine: scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, tracked by this item. Rationale: the
  runner is a Node/TS module invoked by TCE's `npm test` and inherited by consuming game repos
  through their TCE pin, its 1353-line test suite lives beside it, and the framework has no TS
  distribution path for `skill/` scripts. Lifting it into `skill/test/` would need a new
  cross-repo packaging mechanism and would split the runner from its tests, for no gain. The
  diagnostic **and** the bound computation therefore live in exactly one file.
- **D2 — `--timeout-ms` remains a strict, verbatim override** (parent AC3: "`--timeout-ms` still
  wins"). Consequence: the shell must stop pinning the unit bound, otherwise the hybrid bound can
  never apply. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` therefore **drops** `--timeout-ms 300000` from the unit

  `--timeout-ms` raised to the new floor" — a pinned unit bound and load-aware scaling cannot
  both hold; the floor is expressed as the runner constant instead.
- **D3 — Hybrid bound formula.** Static floor **600 s** (2.8× the worst measured green unit stage
  of 217 s, 2× the old 300 s bound); finite ceiling **1200 s** (equal to the browser bound);
  scaling `factor = clamp((load1m / cpuCount) / 0.75, 1, 2)` so `bound = clamp(600 s × factor,
  600 s, 1200 s)` — the floor applies at ≤0.75 load/core, the ceiling at ≥1.5 load/core (e.g. 24
  load on 16 cores). Load is sampled **before** the stage starts (to size the bound) and **at
  abort** (for the diagnostic, per the intake assumption), through one injected seam; on Windows
  the load is unavailable and the floor applies.
- **D4 — Outer budget.** Worst case = unit 1200 + browser 1200 + two `vitest list` pre-flights
  240 + terminology/env pre-checks and orchestration ≈ 60 ⇒ **`.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand: 2700`** (was 1500, which already had zero slack). Accepted trade-off: a
  genuine hang can now take up to ~45 min to abort instead of ~25 min — the deliberate price of

  generosity is visible. (A 900 s ceiling with `timeoutPerCommand: 2400` was the smaller-footprint
  alternative; rejected because 900 s is only 4.1× the worst measured stage and the incident ran
  under sustained load ≥2/core.)
- **D5 — Log shape is frozen.** The `[hang-timeout]` block is enriched; the
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=…` line and the `suite_timeout` notice keep their
  exact shape (release-gate tooling and `run_tests.py` notice classification parse them).
- **D6 — `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` is not touched.** Its log surface is
  owned by SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL (runner JSON discarded); this item only documents the gate
  behaviour in `docs/dev/release-tests.md`.

| 5 | Unit bound wiring and outer gate budget (SA-0MWFX8A7I00883VQ) | feature | shell wiring + budget | AC4, AC5 |

# Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a unit-stage hang abort resumes

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release, I want a unit-stage hang abort to **not** force a full 20+ minute
re-run when the tree is unchanged: the gate should resume from a green cached full-suite entry
within the cache TTL instead of re-executing the whole suite.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The TCE v0.1.24 release gate aborted in the unit stage with a 300 s hang bound (exit 124; no
failing test — host contention, load 35–42 on 16 cores). The per-repo test cache is keyed on
command + git state with a 2 h TTL; the hang **overwrites** the cache entry for that state with
`exit_code: 124`, so a retry on the same tree re-runs every stage from scratch. The release gate
runs `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on the merged dev→main tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hang/abort result (exit `124` from the bounded vitest runner, or any non-zero abort that
  produced no parsable test results) does **not** destroy a green cache entry for the same tree
  state: when a valid green entry exists for the requested command+state within TTL, the cached
  green verdict is served even if a later aborted run wrote to the same key, and the abort is
  still reported (the gate must never *silently* accept an abort as green).
- The resume path is functional end-to-end: re-running the release gate against an unchanged tree
  (same git state, within TTL) after a unit-stage abort consumes the preserved green full-suite
  entry instead of re-executing `npm --silent test`, with the cache TTL gate intact.
- The release gate documents the resume procedure: `run_tests.py`/cache behaviour and the
  operator-visible statement ("the tree is unchanged within TTL — re-run resumes green") are
  described in this repo's release-gate docs and in `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
  comments; no green-entry destruction happens on abort.

# `implement.py start` must not fork a worktree from a local parent branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`

Mirror of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MWFF40700014EE2** (`discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`).
Per the precedent producer decision for **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 ← AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(2026-09-25: "the fix and regression tests live in the SorraAgents counterpart; no
implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix lives here, where
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is.

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`, but
`_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is diverged or cannot
be fetched non-checked-out (`reason: "diverged_or_checked_out"`), and `phase_start` then
forks the worktree from that stale local `dev` anyway (`git_worktree_add(branch,
abs_wt_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <wt> dev`). The child
session inherits a base missing commits already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev` (`e38797b8` local-only,
  duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an unrelated
  `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against pre-fix source and went **red** on a failure
  `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS` still listing the deleted
  `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (`8d1c1aca`) by hand before it could pass its
  gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push to dev
initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and retried"), so this is
recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref whose commits are all contained in
`origin/<parent>` (a fast-forward ancestor of `origin/<parent>`), so a driven child never
starts behind the published base.

## Approach (decided)

The AI_Hell report listed two candidate approaches ("fork from `origin/<parent>`" or
"warn loudly"); the acceptance criteria pin the first and make the second mandatory
reporting, so both are in scope:

1. `_sync_parent_branch` reports `ahead`/`behind` counts (via
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) on every
   skip reason where the counts are computable, in addition to `reason`/`warning`.
2. A new resolver decides the fork base: **fork from
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` whenever the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, which includes the diverged case); otherwise keep the current local-branch
   base.** The local ref is never force-updated — a diverged local `dev` stays exactly as it
   is for the operator to reconcile.
3. `phase_start` records the choice: `report["steps"]["worktree_base"] = {ref, reason,
   ahead, behind}` and an extended "Implementation started"/"resumed" comment naming the base
   ref and, when the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
4. Fail-open is preserved: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch, or a dirty main checkout
   never blocks `start`; when the counts cannot be computed (fetch failed / no remote-tracking
   ref) the local branch remains the base exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded or the worktree is forked
  from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent branch
  was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first changed-scope
  gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh still fails
  open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch.

## Implementation sketch

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): add `ahead`/`behind` to the skipped results
    (`diverged`, `diverged_or_checked_out`, and the other safe-skip paths where computable).
  - New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
    returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`; picks
    `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when behind > 0.
  - `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): pass the resolved ref to `git_worktree_add`, record
    `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, and name it in the start/resume comment (~line 11431).
  - `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): document that the base may be a fully-qualified
    remote-tracking ref; assert the new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` (the
    `--track` upstream must not change — `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`).
- Tests (test-first, new file `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, following
  the hermetic-fixture patterns in `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` /
  `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (start section ~2204-2216, ~4029) and
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~357) — document the base-ref resolution and the new report
  keys/skip reasons.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2` (AI_Hell discovery report; counterpart of this item)
- SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 (completed) — `finish` now fast-forwards local `dev` after the push;
  that closes the *common* stale-local-dev case, leaving the diverged/lock-held skip this
  item fixes.
- SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO — main-checkout lock shared by `start`'s refresh and `finish`.
- SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF — `start` resume-from-worktree path resolved against the main checkout.
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree detection (same "stale base" family).

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a rebase and a red
gate on work someone else already shipped.

# Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

Because concurrent finishes push to the shared `dev` ref, pushes frequently lose the
non-fast-forward race: in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis there were **21** rebase
events. Each rebase rewrites the commit onto a new base, producing a **new tree**, which
misses the tree-keyed gate cache and **re-runs the ~5.4-min full suite** inside the
lock. So a single work item can pay the full-suite cost repeatedly (e.g. AH-0MWEZZE5U,
AH-0MWEYVRUX and others showed 2–3 rebase rounds each).

## Users

- **Operator** running a concurrent fan-out batch into `dev`.
- **Implement-skill session** that loses the push race and today pays another full-suite
  run after rebasing.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session that lost the push race, I want to rebase and push
  without re-running the full suite, because my change content did not change.
- As an operator, I want the number of full-suite gate runs in a batch to stay close to
  the number of work items, not a multiple of it.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a rebased push not to re-run the full suite when the change
content is unchanged, so a lost push race costs seconds, not another 5 minutes.

## Approach (options to weigh)

- Serialise dev pushes (a short push queue / fast-forward retry that rebases only the
  ref, reusing the already-green tree verdict where the tree is provably identical).
- Or key the gate verdict on the **commit's change set / content hash** rather than the
  full tree, so a pure rebase (same diff, different base) reuses the verdict.
- Or batch dev advancement so a batch is rebased once.

## Acceptance criteria

- A push that loses the non-fast-forward race and is rebased onto a new base does
  **not** re-execute the full suite when the tree/diff is provably unchanged (cache
  hit demonstrated in a test).
- The safety property is preserved: a verdict is never reused for a tree/diff that
  actually differs.
- The number of full-suite gate runs for a concurrent fan-out drops measurably
  (recorded before/after).
- An automated test covers the rebase-then-push path reusing a prior green verdict, and
  a negative test proves a genuinely different tree/diff still misses the cache.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The gate must remain evidence about the **pushed** commit: a verdict may only be
  reused when the tested content is provably identical to what is pushed.
- No weakening of the release gate for `dev`/`main`; `scope=full` stays mandatory.
- Cannot rely on changing per-project suite runtime or sharding.
- Out of scope: redesigning the git transport retry policy for auth/transport failures.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  `dev`/`main` pushes and mirrors gate cache entries into the main checkout's
  `.worklog/cache`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` keys cached verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`
  and records `gate-subject` / `gate-verdict` provenance (`tree=`, cache hit/miss + age).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` raises a recoverable non-fast-forward error
  carrying a `rebase_cmd` hint, so the caller rebases onto `origin/dev` and retries —
  producing a new tree and therefore a cache miss today.

## Desired change

A rebased push of provably unchanged content reuses the existing green verdict, so a
lost push race no longer costs another full-suite run.

## Impact

Losing a push race in a concurrent batch costs seconds instead of another five-minute
full-suite run, so a batch's total gate time stops multiplying with the number of
rebases.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — tree-keyed verdict cache, `--gate-commit` binding, `gate-verdict` provenance
- `.githooks/pre-push` — gate invocation and cache mirroring for dev/main pushes
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `PUSH_FAILURE_NON_FAST_FORWARD`, the non-fast-forward exception and its `rebase_cmd` retry path
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` and `tests/test_test_cache.py` — gate cache/reuse tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — push retry / gate documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item extends.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the gate exists.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race handling prior art.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — both reduce gate cost under concurrency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (safety):** reusing a verdict for a different diff would let an untested change
  reach `dev`; mitigation: reuse only on provable content equality, with a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** batching dev advancement is a larger refactor; treat it as the
  fallback option, preferring the verdict-keying change.
- **Assumption:** a pure rebase produces an identical diff (so a change-set key would
  hit) even though the tree SHA differs.
- **Assumption:** the pre-push hook can be told the intended verdict key without
  weakening the "evidence about the pushed commit" property.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 21 rebase events and the
2–3-round repeats (AH-0MWEZZE5U, AH-0MWEYVRUX) in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the
parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the
repository: `.githooks/pre-push` gate invocation and cache mirroring,
`run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache, and the non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry path in
`implement.py`.

# Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis, **9 of 36** implement sessions were effectively
no-ops: 3 messages, ~50 s each — a driven child session that started, loaded the skill,
and exited without doing work (repeated for several child ids, e.g.
AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J, AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414).
Each is cheap individually but indicates the driver is re-spawning children whose work
is blocked or already done, wasting session startup and muddying the pipeline.

## Users

- **Operator** running `/skill:implement <parent>` drive chains: wants every spawned
  session to do real work.
- **Parent (epic) session** that spawns child sessions and must not waste fan-out slots.
- **Child session** that today starts only to discover there is nothing to do.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want the driver to skip children that are already terminal, blocked
  or held, so a batch spends its slots on real work.
- As a parent session, I want each spawned child session to be startable, so the drive
  report is a faithful record of work done.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the driver not to spawn a child session that will immediately
no-op, so fan-out slots and time are not spent on empty runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause identified for the no-op spawns (already-terminal child, blocked child, or
  an id collision).
- `phase_drive` does not spawn a session for a child that is terminal/blocked/held, with
  a test covering the observed pattern.
- Re-running the same batch produces zero no-op sessions.
- An automated test reproduces the observed no-op pattern (terminal/blocked/held child)
  and asserts no session is spawned, alongside a regression test that a genuinely
  startable child is still spawned.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Terminal children are never finished, reset or re-spawned (existing invariant).
- Blocked verdicts must never be overridden: a child held by a producer or an unmet
  dependency edge is a soft wait, not a work item to start.
- `max_child_sessions` / `finish_attempt_limit` bounds stay in force — the fix must not
  introduce unbounded retrying.
- Out of scope: reducing session start-up cost itself (skill loading), and the
  lock/gate performance work in the sibling items.

## Existing state

- `phase_drive` runs `parent` (subprocess-isolated) and spawns a fresh Pi session for
  `next_child`, re-fetching and classifying children via `_is_terminal_child` /
  `_reconcile_spawn_failure` after a failed spawn.
- The blocked verdict already stops the chain **without** spawning (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT),
  so the observed no-ops point at a gap between "what `parent` reported as next" and the
  child's actual state at spawn time (terminal/blocked/held/collision).

## Desired change

Before spawning, `phase_drive` re-validates that the reported `next_child` is genuinely
startable (non-terminal, not blocked, not held) and records the reason instead of
spawning when it is not.

## Impact

Operators stop paying session start-up and pipeline noise for children that do no work,
and a drive report reflects only real sessions — so a fan-out batch's wall-clock is not
padded by empty runs.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` spawn decision, `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `_is_terminal_child`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` and `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — drive-mode tests (spawn/no-spawn assertions, child locks)
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — drive recovery regression coverage
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — drive-phase documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- implement drive: run each epic child in an interactive Herdr pane (same tab) (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40) — pane spawning path.
- Failing finish bound / terminal reconciliation prior art (SA-0MVLJXS7R000XIFL, SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV) referenced in `phase_drive`'s contract.
- Blocked-verdict soft wait (SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT) — the "do not spawn when blocked" precedent this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making spawn decisions optimistic-but-retried would hide the
  real defect; the fix must record *why* a child was skipped.
- **Risk:** a stale `parent` report could cause the driver to skip a genuinely startable
  child, stalling the chain; mitigation: re-fetch the child immediately before the spawn
  decision and keep the existing bounded re-run of `parent`.
- **Assumption:** the no-op sessions were driven by stale/incomplete child state rather
  than by a Pi session-start failure; the root-cause AC must confirm this before fixing.
- **Assumption:** the analysis sample (9 sessions, 3 messages each) is representative of
  driven-child no-ops.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 9 no-op sessions (~50 s,
3 messages) across AH-0MWEXIWBO004GHN6, AH-0MWEXJ7VJ007XTCQ, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J and
AH-0MWF0CSSI007P414, from the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the repository:
`phase_drive` and its spawn/reconcile helpers in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.

> **OPEN QUESTION (root cause):** the analysis recorded the symptom, not the mechanism.
> The implementing session must identify which of (already-terminal child, blocked child,
> id collision, spawn-time state change) caused the observed no-ops before changing
> behaviour — the AC makes this an explicit deliverable rather than an assumption.

# Set assignee per skill

## Problem statement

Skills currently claim work items using the producer identity (`Map`) as the assignee. This makes an agent's claim indistinguishable from a producer hold and prevents the claim reaper from identifying which skill is actually working. Each skill should instead claim with its own name.

## Users

- **Producers** — need to identify which skill is actively working on a work item from the assignee field.
- **Automated systems** (downtime dispatcher, claim reaper) — need accurate assignee attribution to detect and release stale claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Intake skill** — `intake.py start` defaults to `assignee="Intake"` when no explicit assignee is passed; callers that hard-code `--assignee Map` are updated to either omit the flag (using the new default) or use `--assignee Intake`.
2. **Plan skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim in the plan skill's documentation is updated to `--assignee Plan` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
3. **Implement skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Implement` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
4. **Audit skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Audit` (or removed if already using `--assignee ""`).
5. **All other skill documentation** — any remaining references to `--assignee Map` in SKILL.md files are updated to use the appropriate skill name.
6. **Assignee release unchanged** — the assignee-clearing behaviour on every terminal outcome (finish, auto-complete, abort, error) is preserved exactly as-is.

## Impact

Producers and automated systems can now distinguish which skill is actively working on a work item by inspecting the assignee field, and the claim reaper can reliably identify and release stale skill-level claims.

## Constraints

- Only the *claim* assignee changes; release-by-default on every terminal outcome is unaffected.
- The `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT` constant and the `claim_release.py` shared module must continue to treat `Map` as a claimable identity — no changes to shared infrastructure.
- No new work items should be created during the change; only existing skill documentation and any skill scripts that hard-code `Map` are modified.

## Existing state

- The intake skill instructs agents to pass `--assignee Map` to `intake.py start`.
- The `claim_release.py` module defines `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"` and treats it as a normal claim (released on terminal outcomes).
- The plan skill already claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).
- The implement skill also claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).
